mainTopic: Whether a mistaken uprooting (עקירה בטעות) of an offering counts, and then a new משנה on whether the תמידין and the מוספין hold each other back, with the question of which comes first.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier question: the ברייתא's real source for 'what goes up on the מזבח does not come down' is the פסוק 'זאת תורת העולה.' Next, רבה בר בר חנה teaches that כבשי עצרת slaughtered as rams are valid but do not count for the community, and רב says they do count. רב חסדא limits רב to a case where the person only thought they were rams, because a mistaken uprooting (עקירה בטעות) still counts as an uprooting. רבה disagrees and says a mistaken uprooting does not count. רבא and then רבי זירא each challenge רבה, one from a case of mistaken פיגול and one from רבי שמעון's rule about a מנחה. אביי answers both challenges, ending with רבא's rule that a wrong thought which is clearly false does not disqualify. A new משנה then teaches that the תמידין and the מוספין do not hold each other back. It adds רבי שמעון's rules about a missed morning lamb, the incense, and how each Temple vessel is first put into use. The גמרא asks which comes first when the community cannot afford both, and it starts testing רב חסדא's proof from the משנה against the rule that nothing comes before the morning תמיד. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The real source is the verse about the burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers an earlier question: the תנא of the ברייתא relies on the extra wording in 'זאת תורת העולה' as his true source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא is relying on the word-inclusion of 'This is the law of the burnt offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the earlier discussion. It says the ברייתא's rule really comes from the פסוק 'זאת תורת העולה,' and not from the case it mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, there was a difficulty about the source the ברייתא seemed to use for the rule that something already on the מזבח does not come down. The answer is that the real source is the extra-sounding phrase 'זאת תורת העולה,' which is read as including that rule. The other case was only brought as support.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is the law of the burnt offering' (ויקרא 6:2)
included; the פסוק's extra wording adds another case
relies on; leans on as his source
burnt offering; here the word is also read as 'that which goes up'

phrases.english: The tanna, on "This is the law of the burnt offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:2

phrases.english: which includes, he relies on it.
phrases.notes: He means the extra wording of the פסוק includes the rule, and that is his real source.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא אַ״זֹּאת תּוֹרַת הָעֹלָה״ רִיבָּה סְמִיךְ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a difficulty raised before this piece about the ברייתא's source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the source: the real derivation is from a פסוק, and the cited case is only support.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to base its rule on the case it cited.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's real source is the inclusion in 'זאת תורת העולה.'

steps.title: שבועות lambs slaughtered as rams: valid but do not count
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה teaches a ברייתא: כבשי עצרת slaughtered for the sake of rams are valid, but they do not fulfill the owners' obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה taught before רב: The lambs of שבועות that someone slaughtered for the sake of rams are valid, but they do not count for the owners toward their obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבה בר בר חנה quotes a ברייתא about the two שבועות lambs slaughtered under the wrong name, 'rams.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling has two parts. The offerings are kosher, so they can be brought. But the owners, meaning the community, still have not fulfilled their duty to bring כבשי עצרת. This is the normal rule for an offering slaughtered under the wrong name.

keyTerms.meaning: the two lambs brought on שבועות together with the two loaves
rams (older male sheep), a different type of animal from lambs
for the sake of; under the name of
valid; kosher as offerings
the owners of the offering; here the community

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana taught before Rav:
The lambs of Shavuot that one slaughtered for the sake of rams
phrases.notes: עצרת is the גמרא's usual name for שבועות.

phrases.english: are valid,
but they do not count for the owners toward their obligation.
phrases.notes: The 'owners' here is the whole community, since these are communal offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about כבשי עצרת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כבשי עצרת slaughtered for the sake of rams are valid but do not fulfill the community's obligation.

steps.title: רב: they do count
steps.stepSummary: רב rejects the ברייתא's second half and says the lambs do fulfill the obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: They certainly count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב disagrees with what רבה בר בר חנה just taught. He says the lambs do count for the community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב accepts that the offerings are valid. His argument is only with the claim that they do not fulfill the obligation. The doubled word 'עלו ועלו' shows how strongly he holds this view.

keyTerms.meaning: literally 'they went up'; here it means 'they count' or 'they fulfill the obligation'
they certainly count
toward the obligation the owners must fulfill

phrases.english: Rav said to him: they certainly count.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב: עָלוּ וְעָלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the second half of the ruling in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the claim that the lambs do not fulfill the obligation. Their validity is not disputed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב holds that the lambs do satisfy the community's obligation in this case.

steps.title: רב's view fits when he only thought they were rams
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that רב's ruling makes sense when the person thought the animals were rams but still slaughtered them as lambs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: רב's statement makes sense when the person thought they were rams but slaughtered them for the sake of lambs, because lambs were slaughtered for the sake of lambs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא narrows רב's ruling. He describes the exact case where it makes sense that the lambs count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the person was confused about which animal he had. But what he actually said during the slaughter was 'for the sake of lambs,' and they really were lambs. So the intention of the slaughter matched the truth, and the mistaken thought in his head does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: it is reasonable; it makes sense
his statement
he thought; he mistakenly believed
lambs (young male sheep)
since; because

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Rav's statement is reasonable
where he thought they were rams,
and slaughtered them for the sake of lambs,
since lambs were slaughtered for the sake of lambs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִילְּתֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case in which רב's ruling from step 3 holds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the person only mistakenly thought they were rams but slaughtered them as lambs, they count, because lambs were slaughtered as lambs.

steps.title: Slaughtered as rams: they do not count
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא adds that if he thought they were rams and slaughtered them as rams, they do not count, because a mistaken uprooting is still an uprooting.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he thought they were rams and slaughtered them for the sake of rams, they do not count. An uprooting done by mistake is still an uprooting.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא finishes his point. In the case where the person actually slaughtered them 'for rams,' even רב would agree they do not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the slaughter itself was done under the wrong name. That 'uproots' the lambs from their real identity as כבשי עצרת. Even though it only happened because of a mistake, רב חסדא holds that the uprooting still takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: uprooting; removing an offering from its proper identity by slaughtering it under another name
by mistake
is; counts as
a mistaken uprooting still counts as an uprooting

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In both, the person thought the animals were rams. The only difference is what he slaughtered them 'for': lambs (step 4, they count) or rams (here, they do not count).
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the general question of עקירה בטעות, which רבה disputes in the next step.

phrases.english: But where he thought they were rams,
and slaughtered them for the sake of rams, no.
phrases.notes: 'No' means they do not fulfill the community's obligation, even according to רב.

phrases.english: An uprooting in error is an uprooting;

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל כְּסָבוּר אֵילִים, וּשְׁחָטָן לְשׁוּם אֵילִים – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case to step 4 and states the principle behind the difference.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lambs slaughtered for the sake of rams because of a mistake do not count, since עקירה בטעות הויא עקירה.

steps.title: רבה: a mistaken uprooting does not count
steps.stepSummary: רבה disagrees with רב חסדא and holds that an uprooting done by mistake is not an uprooting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: An uprooting done by mistake is not an uprooting.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the opposite view on the principle רב חסדא just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה, a wrong name given only because of a mistake does not remove the offering from its real identity. So even when the lambs were slaughtered 'for rams' by mistake, they can still count. This means רבה can apply רב's ruling more widely than רב חסדא does.

keyTerms.meaning: a mistaken uprooting does not count as an uprooting
not

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on עקירה בטעות. רב חסדא says a mistaken uprooting still uproots, so lambs slaughtered 'for rams' do not count. רבה says a mistaken uprooting does not uproot.

phrases.english: And Rabba said:
an uprooting in error is not an uprooting.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּה אָמַר: עֲקִירָה בְּטָעוּת לָא הָוְיָא עֲקִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the principle רב חסדא stated in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עקירה בטעות is not an עקירה, so a mistaken wrong name does not remove the offering from its identity.

steps.title: רבא quotes a source to challenge רבה
steps.stepSummary: רבא sets up a challenge to רבה. He quotes a משנה about כהנים who made an offering פיגול, and a ברייתא that says their פיגול counts even when they did it by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We can challenge our own ruling. The משנה says that כהנים who made an offering פיגול in the מקדש on purpose must pay. That means if they did it by mistake, they do not have to pay. And a ברייתא taught about this: their פיגול is still פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is setting up a challenge to רבה's ruling from step 6. Here he only quotes the sources; the actual proof comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separates two cases: on purpose (the כהנים pay) and by mistake (they do not pay). The ברייתא adds that even in the mistaken case, the offering itself really becomes פיגול. So a mistaken bad thought still changed the offering. רבא will use this to attack רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering ruined by a wrong thought during the service, such as planning to eat it after its allowed time
Doing something on purpose
Doing something by mistake
Liable (must pay) / exempt (do not have to pay)

phrases.english: Rava said: And we can raise an objection to our teaching:
phrases.notes: 'Our teaching' is רבה's view from step 6, that a mistaken uprooting does not count.

phrases.english: The priests who made an offering piggul in the Temple
phrases.notes: This משנה is in גיטין 54a.

phrases.english: if they did it intentionally, they are liable to pay.
This implies that if they did it unintentionally, they are exempt.
And it was taught about this case: their piggul is piggul.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹתְבִינַן אַשְּׁמַעְתִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against רבה's ruling in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that עקירה בטעות לא הויא עקירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says that פיגול done by mistake still counts. This may show that a mistaken change to an offering is a real change.

steps.title: What kind of mistake is meant? Not knowing it was a sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא is talking about. It rules out the case where the כהן knew it was a חטאת, because that would be on purpose, not by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say the כהן knew it was a חטאת and still had in mind that it was a שלמים, is that 'by mistake'? That is on purpose!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is narrowing down the case in the ברייתא. It throws out the first possibility, which prepares the way for רבא's proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת may only be eaten for one day, but a שלמים may be eaten for two days. Thinking 'שלמים' about a חטאת means planning to eat it too late, and that makes it פיגול. If the כהן knew it was a חטאת and still thought this, he acted on purpose, so this cannot be the 'mistake' case.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What case is this?
If you say (offering a possibility that will be rejected)
Sin offering, eaten for only one day and a night
Peace offering, eaten for two days and a night
Has a thought or intention during the service

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say that he knew it was a sin offering,
and he had the intention that it was for the sake of a peace offering,
phrases.notes: A שלמים is eaten for an extra day, so this thought means eating the חטאת too late.

phrases.english: Is this unintentional?! They were acting intentionally!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִילֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts defining the 'mistake' case from the ברייתא quoted in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of 'mistaken' פיגול is the ברייתא talking about?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not a case where the כהן knew it was a חטאת, because that would be on purpose.

steps.title: So the priest thought it was a peace offering, which proves a mistaken uprooting counts
steps.stepSummary: The only option left is that the כהן thought the חטאת was a שלמים. Since the ברייתא says it is still פיגול, a mistaken עקירה must count, which goes against רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it a case where he thought it was a שלמים and had in mind that it was a שלמים? And the ברייתא teaches that their פיגול is פיגול. This shows that a mistaken עקירה is a real עקירה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his challenge. He says the ברייתא must be talking about a כהן who honestly thought the animal was a שלמים, and that case is still פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case matches רב חסדא's case from step 5: the person had the wrong animal in mind and acted on that mistake. If the ברייתא says it becomes פיגול, then a mistaken change of the offering's identity counts. That supports רב חסדא and goes against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it...? (introducing the only option left)
This shows that... (drawing a conclusion)
Uprooting (changing) an offering's identity by mistake

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main attack on רבה's view, so the sugya now turns on how to read this ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not where he thought it was a peace offering,
and he had the intention that it was for the sake of a peace offering,
and it teaches: their piggul is piggul.
Apparently, a mistaken uprooting is an uprooting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו דִּכְסָבוּר שְׁלָמִים הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the option left over after step 8 to complete the challenge against רבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only way to read 'by mistake' is that the כהן thought it was a שלמים. Since it is still פיגול, a mistaken עקירה must count.

steps.title: אביי: he knew it was a sin offering but thought it was allowed
steps.stepSummary: אביי defends רבה. The כהן really did know it was a חטאת. His mistake was thinking he was allowed to have that thought, so the ברייתא proves nothing about a mistaken עקירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Really, he knew it was a חטאת and had in mind that it was a שלמים. The case is where he says it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבא's challenge. He goes back to the case the גמרא rejected in step 8 and explains why it can still be called 'by mistake.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'mistake' in the ברייתא is about the law, not about the animal. The כהן knew exactly what offering he had, so his עקירה was done knowingly. He just wrongly thought this thought was allowed. That makes him a שוגג who does not have to pay, but his עקירה was not a mistaken one, so רבה's rule is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (keeping the case that was rejected)
He says it is permitted: a mistake about the law, not about the facts

steps.whatToRemember: There are two kinds of 'mistake.' Mistaking the facts (thinking a חטאת is a שלמים) is a mistaken עקירה, and רבה says it does not count. Mistaking the law (knowing it is a חטאת but thinking the thought is allowed) still counts as a real עקירה, even though the כהן is called a שוגג and does not have to pay.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume every 'שוגג' means the person got the facts wrong. Here the כהן knew the facts; he only thought the law allowed what he did.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Actually, it is where he knew that it was a sin offering,
and he had the intention that it was for the sake of a peace offering,
and it is where he says that it is 'permitted.'
phrases.notes: He means the כהן wrongly thought he was allowed to have this thought.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 9 by bringing back the case rejected in step 8, with a new explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the 'mistake' is about the law, not the facts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'By mistake' had to mean the כהן thought the חטאת was a שלמים, so a mistaken עקירה would count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן knew it was a חטאת and only thought the thought was allowed. His עקירה was knowing, so רבה's rule still stands.

steps.title: רבי זירא quotes רבי שמעון on a מנחה taken for the wrong purpose
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא opens a challenge to רבה by quoting a ברייתא: רבי שמעון says every מנחה whose handful was taken שלא לשמה is kosher and even counts for the owner's obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא raised an objection: רבי שמעון says, all מנחות whose handful was taken for the wrong purpose are kosher, and they count for the owners as fulfilling their obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא starts a new challenge against רבה by quoting a ruling of רבי שמעון. This is only the opening; the actual attack comes after the גמרא figures out what case is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually an offering done שלא לשמה is kosher but does not count for the owner's obligation. רבי שמעון says a מנחה is different: it fully counts. רבי זירא will try to use this to show something about a mistaken עקירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Flour offerings brought in the בית המקדש
The כהן took out a handful (קמיצה) of the flour, the main service of a מנחה
Not for their own purpose; done with the thought of a different kind of offering
Count for the owner as fulfilling his obligation

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira raised an objection:
phrases.notes: He is challenging רבה, who said a mistaken uprooting does not count.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מְנָחוֹת שֶׁנִּקְמְצוּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן – כְּשֵׁרוֹת,
phrases.english: all meal offerings whose handful was taken not for their sake are valid,
and they count for the owners as their obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי deflected רבא's challenge, רבי זירא brings a second challenge against רבה from a different source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that a mistaken עקירה is not an עקירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The גמרא will show that רבי שמעון's case must be one where the כהן made a mistake. The offering stays kosher only because its preparation proves what it is. That implies that elsewhere, where nothing proves it, a mistaken עקירה does count, which goes against רבה.

steps.title: Why a מנחה is different from an animal offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains: a מנחה's preparation shows what kind it is, so a wrong thought is obviously false. Animal offerings are all done the same way, so the thought is what decides.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because מנחות are not like animal offerings. If someone takes a handful from a מחבת for the sake of a מרחשת, the way it was made proves it is a מחבת. If he takes from a dry one for the sake of one mixed with oil, the way it was made proves it is dry. But animal offerings are not like this: there is one way of שחיטה for all of them, one way of קבלה for all of them, one way of זריקה for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is still talking. It gives the reason a wrong thought does not hurt a מנחה: you can see what kind of מנחה it is just by looking at it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחבת is hard and a מרחשת is soft; a dry מנחה has no oil and a mixed one does. So when the כהן thinks it is a different kind, the facts show his thought is wrong. With animals, every offering is slaughtered and its blood is caught and thrown the same way, so the thought really can change things.

keyTerms.meaning: A מנחה made in a flat pan, so it comes out hard
A מנחה made in a deep pan, so it comes out soft
A dry מנחה with no oil, like a sinner's מנחה
A מנחה mixed with oil
Its own preparation proves what it is

steps.whyThisMatters: This reason (the preparation shows what it is) is the key idea the גמרא will now examine to see which case רבי שמעון is talking about.

phrases.english: for meal offerings are not like animal offerings,
since one who takes a handful from a shallow-pan offering for the sake of a deep-pan offering –
its preparation proves that it is a shallow-pan offering,
a dry offering for the sake of one mixed with oil –
its preparation proves that it is dry.
But with animal offerings it is not so,
there is one slaughtering for all of them,
one collecting of the blood for all of them,
one sprinkling for all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין הַמְּנָחוֹת דּוֹמוֹת לַזְּבָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבי שמעון's ruling quoted in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wrong thought does not disqualify a מנחה from counting for its owner, because its visible preparation shows its true type, unlike animal offerings, which are all done the same way.

steps.title: Ruling out the case where the כהן knew it was a מחבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רבי שמעון means. If the כהן knew it was a מחבת and still took the handful for a מרחשת, the visible preparation should not help, since he is uprooting it on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say he knew it was a מחבת and took the handful for the sake of a מרחשת, then even if its preparation proves what it is, so what? He is uprooting it on purpose!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which case רבי שמעון is talking about, and rules out the first option. This sets up the next move, where only the mistaken case will be left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהן knew the truth and still decided to call it a מרחשת, that is a full, on-purpose עקירה, and seeing the pan should not fix it. So רבי שמעון's reason only makes sense if the כהן was mistaken. This mirrors step 8, where the גמרא also threw out the 'he knew' case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact facts?
If you say (suggests an option that will be rejected)
What of it? So what?
Uprooted; changed the offering's identity by his thought

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a מנחה on purpose is disqualified here; it is only showing that the 'he knew' case cannot be what רבי שמעון's reason is talking about.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If you say that he knew it was a shallow-pan offering,
and he took its handful for the sake of a deep-pan offering –
even though its preparation proves it, what of it?
He is actually uprooting it!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִילֵּימָא דְּיָדַע דְּמַחֲבַת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which case the ברייתא in steps 11-12 is talking about, and rules out the on-purpose case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי שמעון's case is one where the כהן knew the מנחה's true type or one where he was mistaken.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'he knew' option is rejected because then he is uprooting it on purpose, and the visible preparation should not matter. Step 14 gives the remaining reading, and steps 15-16 bring back the 'he knew' reading with an answer.

steps.title: The case must be an honest mistake, which goes against רבה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא concludes that רבי שמעון's case must be a כהן who mistakenly thought the מנחה was a מרחשת. That would imply that a mistaken עקירה normally does count, against רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be that he thought it was a מרחשת, took the handful for a מרחשת, and was wrong. Only here is it kosher, because its preparation shows what it really is. But in general, an uprooting done by mistake does count as an uprooting.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא finishes his challenge. He says רבי שמעון's case must be about an honest mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 ruled out a case where the כהן knew the truth, so the only case left is a mistake. רבי שמעון says the offering is kosher only because its preparation shows the truth. That suggests that without such proof, a mistaken עקירה would count, and רבה holds that it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A מנחה made in a deep pan; its dough is soft and loose
A מנחה made in a shallow pan; its dough is firm
Its preparation proves what it is
Uprooting an offering's identity by mistake, not on purpose

steps.confusionAlert: Here the challenger is not saying the offering is פסול. He agrees it is kosher. He is drawing a conclusion from the reason it is kosher: only the visible proof saves it, so in other cases a mistake would count.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not where he thought it was a deep-pan offering,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא קָמֵיץ לָהּ לְשׁוּם מַרְחֶשֶׁת, וּטְעָה,
phrases.english: so he took its handful for the sake of a deep-pan offering, and he was mistaken?
It is only here that it is kosher, because its preparation proves what it is,
which implies that in general,
a mistaken uprooting is considered an uprooting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו דִּכְסָבוּר מַרְחֶשֶׁת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles on the only remaining reading of רבי שמעון after step 13 rejected the case where the כהן knew the truth.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that a mistaken עקירה does not count as an עקירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only the visible proof makes the mistaken מנחה kosher, then where there is no such proof, a mistaken עקירה would count. That contradicts רבה.

steps.title: אביי: the כהן knew it was a מחבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רבי שמעון's case really is a כהן who knew it was a מחבת and still took the handful for a מרחשת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Really, he knew it was a מחבת, and he took the handful for the sake of a מרחשת.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבה. He goes back to the reading that step 13 rejected: the כהן knew the truth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהן knew the truth, the case has nothing to do with a mistaken עקירה, so it cannot prove anything against רבה. אביי still has to answer step 13's question about why a deliberate change does not ruin the offering. He does that in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; actually (used to keep a reading that was just questioned)
Takes the handful (קמיצה) from a מנחה

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Actually, it is where he knew that it was a shallow-pan offering,
and he took its handful for the sake of a deep-pan offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם דְּיָדַע דְּמַחֲבַת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 14's conclusion by bringing back the reading that step 13 had questioned.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the change was on purpose, not a mistake.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's case must be an honest mistake, which would prove that a mistaken עקירה counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a deliberate change, so it proves nothing about a mistaken עקירה.

steps.title: A thought that is clearly false does not disqualify
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers step 13's question with a rule: the Torah disqualifies only a wrong thought that cannot be recognized as false, not one that can.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for what you asked, "So what if its preparation proves what it is?" רבא follows his own reasoning. רבא said: The Torah disqualified a thought that cannot be recognized. It did not disqualify a thought that can be recognized.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers step 13's question: why is a deliberate wrong thought harmless here? He brings a general rule from רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 asked how the visible preparation could help when the כהן changed the offering on purpose. The answer is that the Torah only makes a wrong thought count when nothing shows it to be false. With a מחבת, everyone can see the thought "מרחשת" is false, so the thought has no effect, even if it was deliberate.

keyTerms.meaning: A thought that can be recognized as false, because the facts show the truth
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Following his own reasoning; consistent with his known view

steps.whatToRemember: A wrong thought disqualifies an offering only when nothing visible shows it is false. When the preparation clearly shows the truth, the thought is ignored, even if it was on purpose.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule removes the proof against רבה. רבי שמעון's ruling comes from how visible the falsehood is, not from whether the כהן made a mistake.

phrases.english: And as for what you said:
phrases.notes: He is going back to the question from step 13.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מַעֲשֶׂיהָ מוֹכִיחִין עָלֶיהָ מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: "If its preparation proves what it is, what of it?"
Rava follows his own reasoning,
as Rava said:
A thought that is not recognizable as false, the Merciful One disqualified;
a thought that is recognizable as false, the Merciful One did not disqualify.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְקָא אָמְרַתְּ: כִּי מַעֲשֶׂיהָ מוֹכִיחִין עָלֶיהָ מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer by explaining why a deliberate change is harmless in this case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general principle explaining the ruling: only a thought that cannot be seen to be false disqualifies.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A deliberate change of identity should ruin the offering even if the preparation shows the truth.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the thought is visibly false, the Torah ignores it, so the offering is kosher and counts for the owner.

steps.title: New משנה: daily and additional offerings do not hold each other back
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that the תמידין and the מוספין do not hold each other back, the מוספין do not hold one another back, and a missed morning lamb does not stop the afternoon lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The daily offerings do not hold back the additional offerings. The additional offerings do not hold back the daily offerings. The additional offerings do not hold back one another. If they did not bring the lamb in the morning, they should bring it in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. If one required offering was missed, can the others still be brought?
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעכבין means "hold back": one thing being missing stops the other from being done. The משנה says each of these offerings stands on its own. Missing one never prevents bringing the others, including the afternoon תמיד when the morning one was skipped.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily offerings: one lamb in the morning and one in the afternoon
The additional offerings brought on שבת, ראש חודש and יום טוב
Hold back; one being missing prevents the other
In the afternoon, the time of the second תמיד

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הַתְּמִידִין אֵין מְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַמּוּסָפִין,
phrases.english: MISHNA: The daily offerings do not hold back the additional offerings,
nor do the additional offerings hold back the daily offerings,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הַמּוּסָפִין מְעַכְּבִין זֶה אֶת זֶה.
phrases.english: nor do the additional offerings hold back one another.
If they did not offer a lamb in the morning,
they should offer one in the afternoon.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַתְּמִידִין אֵין מְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַמּוּסָפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of עקירה in a מנחה ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Missing the תמידין, the מוספין, or one of several מוספין does not prevent bringing the others, and a missed morning תמיד does not stop the afternoon תמיד.

steps.title: A missed morning lamb only fails to block the afternoon lamb when the miss was not on purpose
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון limits the משנה's rule. If the כהנים skipped the morning lamb on purpose, they may not bring the afternoon lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: When does this rule apply? When they were forced or made a mistake. But if they skipped the morning lamb on purpose, they should not offer the afternoon lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון adds a condition to the rule from step 17 that a missed morning lamb does not stop the afternoon lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a missed morning תמיד does not stop the afternoon תמיד. רבי שמעון says this is true only when the miss was forced or a mistake. If the כהנים skipped it on purpose, the afternoon lamb is also not brought.

keyTerms.meaning: Forced; stopped by something outside their control
Acting by mistake, without meaning to
Acting on purpose
A lamb, here the lamb of the daily תמיד offering
In the afternoon, the time of the second daily offering

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי שמעון as arguing with the whole משנה. He agrees that a missed morning lamb usually does not block the afternoon lamb. He only adds the case where the miss was on purpose.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: When does this apply?
phrases.notes: "This" is the rule from the last step: a missed morning lamb does not stop the afternoon lamb.

phrases.english: At a time when they were forced or acting by mistake,
but if they acted on purpose
and did not offer a lamb in the morning,
they should not offer one in the afternoon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי שמעון אימתי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to step 17's rule about the morning and afternoon lambs
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the morning תמיד was skipped on purpose, the afternoon תמיד is not offered. If it was missed by force or by mistake, the afternoon תמיד is still offered.

steps.title: Missed morning incense is still burned in the afternoon
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the morning קטורת was not burned, the afternoon קטורת is still burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they did not burn incense in the morning, they should burn it in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from the lambs to the incense. Missing the morning incense does not cancel the afternoon incense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קטורת was burned twice a day, half in the morning and half in the afternoon. Just like the lambs, the morning half does not hold back the afternoon half. This line also sets up רבי שמעון's comment in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The spice incense burned on the inner golden altar each morning and afternoon
They burned (as an offering)

phrases.english: If they did not burn incense in the morning,
they should burn it in the afternoon.

steps.triggerLanguage: לא הקטירו קטורת בבוקר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same idea from the lambs to the incense
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A missed morning קטורת does not stop the afternoon קטורת from being burned.

steps.title: The whole amount of incense was burned in the afternoon, and how each Temple vessel is first put into use
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the whole amount of קטורת was burned in the afternoon. He explains this with a list of how each Temple vessel is first put into use.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: And all of it was offered in the afternoon. This is because the golden altar is first put into use only with the incense of spices. The altar of burnt offerings is first put into use only with the morning תמיד. The שולחן is first put into use only with the לחם הפנים on שבת. The מנורה is first put into use only with its seven lamps in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון adds to the incense rule: in this case the full amount was burned in the afternoon. He supports this with the rules for first putting each vessel into use (חינוך).
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, a new golden altar is first put into use with the afternoon קטורת, so the whole measure goes in the afternoon. The outer altar, by contrast, is first put into use with the morning תמיד. This list explains why incense and lambs are not treated the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Putting a new Temple vessel into use for the first time (חִנּוּךְ)
The golden (inner) altar, where the קטורת is burned
The altar of burnt offerings (the outer altar), where the תמיד is offered
The morning daily offering
The twelve breads placed on the שולחן every שבת
The seven-branched lamp in the היכל

steps.whatToRemember: Each Temple vessel has a set first service that puts it into use. The outer altar starts with the morning תמיד, while the golden altar and the מנורה start in the afternoon.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list is the background for why the incense and the lambs are treated differently when the morning service was missed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: וְכוּלָּהּ הָיְתָה קְרֵיבָה בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: And all of it was offered in the afternoon,
phrases.notes: "All of it" means the full measure of incense, both the morning half and the afternoon half.

phrases.english: for they do not put the golden altar into use
except with the incense of spices,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִזְבַּח הָעוֹלָה אֶלָּא בְּתָמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר,
phrases.english: and not the altar of burnt offerings except with the morning daily offering,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הַשּׁוּלְחָן אֶלָּא בְּלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: and not the Table except with the showbread on Shabbat,
and not the Menorah
except with its seven lamps in the afternoon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי שמעון וכולה היתה קריבה בין הערבים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to step 19's incense rule and gives a reason
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The full measure of קטורת is burned in the afternoon. Each Temple vessel is first put into use with a set service: the golden altar with קטורת, the outer altar with the morning תמיד, the שולחן with לחם הפנים on שבת, and the מנורה with its seven lamps in the afternoon.

steps.title: A community that can't afford both: daily offerings or additional offerings first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins. רבי חייא בר אבין asks רב חסדא which comes first for a community that cannot bring both the תמידין and the מוספין.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי חייא בר אבין asked רב חסדא: If a community does not have enough for both the daily offerings and the additional offerings, which of them comes first?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a practical question that builds on the משנה. This step sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that the תמידין and מוספין do not hold each other back, so each one can be brought without the other. That raises a new question: if there is only enough for one, which one gets priority?

keyTerms.meaning: The community as a whole, which pays for public offerings
The additional offerings brought on שבת, ראש חודש and holidays
Comes first; has priority

phrases.english: GEMARA

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין מֵרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin asked of Rav Chisda:
A community that does not have daily offerings and additional offerings,
phrases.notes: He means they don't have enough animals or money for both, only for one.

phrases.english: which of them comes first?

steps.triggerLanguage: בעא מיניה רבי חייא בר אבין מרב חסדא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא with a question built on step 17's rule that תמידין and מוספין do not hold each other back
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When a community can afford only one, which has priority: the תמידין or the מוספין?

steps.title: What case is the question about? Not today's offerings against today's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רבי חייא בר אבין meant. It cannot be today's תמידין against today's מוספין, because the תמידין obviously come first: they are both more frequent (תדיר) and holy (מקודש).
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say it is today's daily offerings against today's additional offerings, that is obvious. The daily offerings come first, because they are more frequent and also holy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what exact case the question in step 21 was about. It rules out the simplest case because its answer is obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two reasons one offering can come first: it is more frequent (תדיר), or it is holier (מקודש). When today's תמידין face today's מוספין, the תמידין have both reasons, so there is nothing to ask. The question must be about some other case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?
If you say (a suggestion the גמרא is about to reject)
It is obvious
Frequent: something that happens more often, which comes first
Holier: something with more holiness, which also comes first

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
phrases.notes: This is asking about רבי חייא בר אבין's question from the previous step.

phrases.english: If we say the daily offerings of that day
and the additional offerings of that day,
it is obvious that the daily offerings take preference,
since they are both frequent and sanctified!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא תְּמִידִין דְּיוֹמֵיהּ וּמוּסָפִין דְּיוֹמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the case behind the question asked in step 21 and rules out the simple reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exact case was רבי חייא בר אבין asking about?

steps.title: The real question: tomorrow's daily offerings against today's additional offerings
steps.stepSummary: The question must be about tomorrow's תמידין against today's מוספין. The תמידין are more frequent, but the מוספין are holier. So which one wins?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is tomorrow's daily offerings against today's additional offerings. Do the daily offerings come first because they are more frequent? Or do the additional offerings come first because they are holier?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real case behind the question. Now the two reasons for going first pull in opposite directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Today's תמידין are already covered. The only choice is between tomorrow's תמידין and today's מוספין. The תמידין still have the advantage of תדיר, but the מוספין belong to a holy day, so they have the advantage of מקודש. That is why this is a real question.

keyTerms.meaning: Tomorrow
Today, now
They take preference, they come first
Perhaps

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a real clash between the two rules for what comes first: תדיר against מקודש.

phrases.english: Rather, the daily offerings for tomorrow
phrases.notes: The idea is that they already have enough for today's תמידין. The choice is only about the extra animals.

phrases.english: and the additional offerings of today:
are the daily offerings preferred, since they are frequent,
or perhaps the additional offerings are preferred,
since they are sanctified?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, תְּמִידִין דְּלִמְחַר וּמוּסָפִין דְּהָאִידָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the simple case in step 22, gives the real case of the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question is about tomorrow's תמידין (frequent) against today's מוספין (holier).

steps.title: רב חסדא points to our משנה for an answer
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the question is already answered in the משנה: the תמידין and the מוספין do not hold each other back, and the מוספין do not hold one another back.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You learned it in the משנה. The daily offerings do not hold back the additional offerings, the additional offerings do not hold back the daily offerings, and the additional offerings do not hold one another back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא tries to answer the question from our own משנה. Here he only quotes it. The גמרא will now work out what it proves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא brings the משנה as a source that should settle the question. The proof depends on what case the משנה is talking about. That is exactly what the גמרא checks in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: You learned it already (in a משנה)
Hold back, prevent
One another

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it:
phrases.notes: רב חסדא is speaking to רבי חייא בר אבין. He quotes the משנה from step 17.

phrases.english: The daily offerings do not prevent the additional offerings,
and the additional offerings do not prevent the daily offerings,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הַמּוּסָפִין מְעַכְּבִין זֶה אֶת זֶה.
phrases.english: and the additional offerings do not prevent one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, תְּנֵיתוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 by pointing to the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The question of tomorrow's תמידין against today's מוספין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: תמידין and מוספין do not hold each other back.

steps.title: The משנה cannot just be about which goes first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the משנה means. If they have enough animals and the משנה only teaches order, that is a problem. A ברייתא already teaches that nothing may come before the morning תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say they have enough animals and the משנה is about which one goes first, there is a problem. A ברייתא teaches: How do we know that nothing may come before the morning תמיד? The פסוק says: "And he shall arrange the burnt offering on it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the case of the משנה that רב חסדא quoted. It rejects the idea that the משנה is about order when there are enough animals. The next step completes this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there are enough animals for everything, the only question would be which one is offered first. But that is not open: the ברייתא learns from a פסוק that the morning תמיד always comes first. So the משנה must be teaching something else, and the גמרא will need another explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: To go first, to come before

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the morning תמיד and the מוספין are equal in timing. The ברייתא says the morning תמיד always comes first, so the משנה cannot be just about order.

steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the משנה as being about order when there are enough animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה meant that, with enough animals, the order does not matter and either may go first, it would clash with the ברייתא. The ברייתא learns from a פסוק that nothing may come before the morning תמיד.

steps.title: רבא explains that "the burnt offering" means the first offering of the day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its challenge with רבא's explanation of the ברייתא: "הָעֹלָה" means the first עולה of the day, the morning תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: "The burnt offering" means the first burnt offering of the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its challenge from step 25. It shows where the ברייתא's rule comes from: רבא reads the word "הָעֹלָה" as pointing to the first burnt offering of the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ה ("THE" burnt offering) points to one specific עולה, the first one of the day, which is the morning תמיד. So the Torah requires that nothing, not even the מוספין, be offered before the morning תמיד. The משנה therefore cannot mean that, with enough animals, the order does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: "The" burnt offering. The word "the" points to one specific offering.
The first burnt offering of the day, meaning the morning תמיד.
The daily morning offering, which must come before every other offering of the day.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that the morning תמיד is always the first offering of the day. That rule is what pushes the גמרא to read the משנה in a different way.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
"The burnt offering" means the first burnt offering!
phrases.notes: This is the word from the פסוק "וְעָרַךְ עָלֶיהָ הָעֹלָה" (ויקרא 6:5). "The" points to the first עולה of the day, the morning תמיד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge of step 25 by explaining how the ברייתא learns that nothing comes before the morning תמיד.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that no offering may come before the morning תמיד, which is the basis of the challenge against reading the משנה as only teaching order.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's reading of the word "הָעֹלָה" in the פסוק (ויקרא 6:5) as the first burnt offering of the day.
